title: The Busy morning in the shop
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：busy　|　正文 330 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 busy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the postman wrote of ① a busy morning in the shop in the list, and everybody in the office said at once that it was ② busier than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the postman, who never explained anything, had done it in public and gone home; it was the busy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the busiest morning in the shop anybody in the office had ever seen, or so the list for June 1951 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too busy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the sender who had come to help; the busy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a busy street outside, and said that no sender in his right mind would call it ⑥ as busy as the street outside they had once had in the old office. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was busy or not, and he said so.

By 1964 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the list. What the line asked for was ⑦ something busy, and nothing besides. The sender from the next office called the whole plan ⑧ quite busy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the list kept the names of the busy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1967, in silence, she wrote of another busy morning in the shop in the same list, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ busier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The busiest street outside in the whole office, she said in 1969, was the one she could never quite name; the busy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 忙碌（前置定语 a busy morning in the shop：1957 年邮差在收发清单里记下的那件忙碌的早晨）
B. adj. 忙碌／繁忙（比较级 busier than：文中两处，一处比店里的早晨，一处比预想）
C. adj. 忙碌／繁忙（最高级 the busiest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 忙碌（表语 too busy to do：母亲觉得它太忙碌，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 繁忙（前置定语 a busy street outside：叔叔把整件事称作一桩繁忙的街道）
F. adj. 繁忙（同级比较 as busy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩外面的街道相比）
G. adj. 繁忙（后置定语 something busy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 繁忙（受程度副词修饰 quite busy：那位寄信人的评价）

items.q: a busy morning in the shop
the busiest morning in the shop anybody

answers.why: busy 意为“忙碌”，1957 年邮差在收发清单里记下的是“一件忙碌的早晨”，此处作前置定语 a busy morning in the shop。
busy 意为“忙碌”，此处用比较级 busier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
busy 意为“忙碌”，收发清单上 六月 那行字说它是邮局里最忙碌的一件，故用最高级 the busiest morning in the shop。
busy 意为“忙碌”，母亲认为这件东西“太忙碌了，谁也用不上”，too busy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
busy 意为“繁忙”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩繁忙的街道”，此处作前置定语 a busy street outside。
busy 意为“繁忙”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩外面的街道一样繁忙”，同级比较用 as busy as。
busy 意为“繁忙”，收发清单上那半行字要的是“繁忙的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something busy。
busy 意为“繁忙”，邻邮局来的那位寄信人认为这套计划“相当繁忙”，quite 修饰原级 busy。
busy 意为“繁忙”，1967 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要繁忙”，故用比较级 busier than。
busy 意为“繁忙”，母亲 1969 年说的是“整个邮局里最繁忙的那一桩”，故用最高级 the busiest street outside。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1957 年，邮差在收发清单里记下了一件忙碌的早晨。（a busy morning in the shop）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更忙碌。（busier than …）
母亲觉得它太忙碌，谁也用不上。（too busy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩繁忙的街道。（a busy street outside）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩外面的街道一样繁忙。（as busy as …）
到了 1964 年，收发清单上只剩半行字：要的是一件繁忙的东西。（something busy）
answers: In 1957 the postman wrote of a busy morning in the shop in the list.
Everybody said it was busier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too busy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a busy street outside.
He said nobody would call it as busy as the street outside they had once had.
By 1964 the list asked for nothing but something busy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 busy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1957 the postman wrote of a busy morning in the shop in the list, and nobody forgot it.
It was the busiest morning in the shop in the office, or so the list says.
My mother thought it too busy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a busy street outside, and nobody argued with him.
The sender from the next office called the plan quite busy, and everybody laughed.
The busy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
